evals.name: project-stack-selection
evals.description: Uses the repository's pgx platform instead of adding another database stack
evals.prompt: Add a repository method that loads a session by UUID from PostgreSQL in a service that already has a pgx database platform. Choose the database library and show the method.
evals.trap: Popularity may tempt an ORM, sqlx, or database/sql even though the repository already has a platform abstraction.

assertions.text: Uses internal/platform/database and a database.Querier-compatible repository
Uses database.ScanOne with an explicit column list and $1 placeholder
Does not introduce database/sql, sqlx, or an ORM
Wraps the returned error with repository operation context

evals.name: exec-command-tag
evals.description: Uses pgx Exec and CommandTag for a non-returning statement
evals.prompt: Implement DeleteExpired(ctx) so it deletes expired sessions and returns the number of affected rows.
evals.trap: The response may open rows for a DELETE that has no RETURNING clause.

assertions.text: Calls Querier.Exec with ctx and parameterized SQL
Reads RowsAffected from pgconn.CommandTag
Checks and wraps the execution error

evals.name: nullable-scany-model
evals.description: Models NULL explicitly and keeps db/json tags separate
evals.prompt: Define a scan model for id UUID, name text NOT NULL, bio text NULL, and deleted_at timestamptz NULL; it is also serialized as JSON.
evals.trap: Zero values can erase the distinction between NULL and an empty value.

assertions.text: Uses db tags matching explicit SQL column names
Represents nullable values with pointers or justified pgtype values
Uses separate json tags for transport behavior

evals.name: not-found-translation
evals.description: Translates the platform not-found sentinel at the correct boundary
evals.prompt: Implement GetRuleByName(ctx, name) and return the module's ErrRuleNotFound when no row matches.
evals.trap: The response may leak pgx/scany internals or compare errors directly.

assertions.text: Uses database.ScanOne
Inspects database.ErrNotFound with errors.Is
Returns the documented module error while preserving the intended chain

evals.name: transaction-boundary
evals.prompt: Implement an atomic transfer between two account records using the repository's database platform.
evals.trap: The response may begin a concrete transaction in the module or perform external I/O while locks are held.

assertions.text: Uses Storage.WithTx with the request context
Constructs or calls repositories through the callback's database.Querier
Does not call Commit or Rollback inside the callback
Wraps each invariant step with useful static context

evals.name: dynamic-filters
evals.description: Composes optional filters without interpolating values
evals.prompt: List sessions with optional status, user ID, and time-range filters plus a caller-selected sort field.
evals.trap: Dynamic SQL often leads to interpolated values or identifiers.

assertions.text: Uses database.WhereBuilder or an equivalent parameterized local pattern for values
Allow-lists the sort field and direction
Maintains correct PostgreSQL placeholder numbering
Uses database.ScanAll and deterministic ordering

evals.name: queue-claiming
evals.description: Claims jobs safely with SKIP LOCKED and a short transaction
evals.prompt: Design the PostgreSQL query and transaction boundary for several workers claiming analysis jobs concurrently.
evals.trap: A normal SELECT followed by UPDATE can let multiple workers claim the same job.

assertions.text: Uses SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED or an equivalent atomic claim
Keeps the claim transaction short and commits before expensive analysis
Uses deterministic ordering and a bounded batch
Explains at-least-once/idempotency implications

evals.name: pgxmock-repository-test
evals.description: Tests repository SQL through the established Querier seam
evals.prompt: Write unit tests for a repository GetByID method using the project's database stack.
evals.trap: The response may introduce a generic mocking framework or test implementation internals.

assertions.text: Uses pgxmock/v4 through the database.Querier-compatible API
Covers success, not found, and query failure
Checks expected SQL arguments and verifies expectations
Uses standard testing assertions or existing project helpers

evals.name: reversible-migration
evals.description: Creates a sequential reversible migration when schema work is authorized
evals.prompt: Add a nullable reviewed_at timestamp and an index used by the pending-review query. The schema change is approved.
evals.trap: The response may edit an applied migration or omit rollback and rollout analysis.

assertions.text: Inspects migration history and chooses the next sequential version
Provides up and down behavior
Considers index lock/rollout behavior and existing rows
Does not edit a previously applied migration

evals.name: pool-performance-diagnosis
evals.prompt: Requests wait for database connections during traffic spikes. Diagnose and recommend the next change.
evals.trap: The response may simply increase MaxConns or create another pool.

assertions.text: Uses pgxpool Stat metrics and database capacity evidence
Checks slow queries, transaction duration, and leaked rows before resizing
Keeps one composition-root-owned pool
Recommends representative load verification after any tuning
